newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt firm, Loewenbraeu to set up brewery.
newsitem.headline: Egypt firm, Loewenbraeu to set up brewery.

text.p: German brewery Loewenbraeu and Egyptian firm Orascom Touristic Establishments are setting up a 90 million pound ($26 million) brewery in the Red Sea resort of el-Gouna, a senior Orascom official said on Sunday.
President Samih Sawiris told Reuters that construction has already begun on the plant, which is expected to start production by the end of this year.
"We have an agreement with Loewenbraeu to provide us with technical expertise and they are contemplating going in with 20 percent," Sawiris said.
Orascom holds a 51 percent majority in the brewery and other Egyptian investors own unspecified stakes, he added.
It will the first private-sector brewery built in Egypt at least since the 1960s. Its only rival is recently privatised Pyramids Breweries (Al-Ahram Beverages).
Pyramids Breweries produces Stella, now the country's only beer. Stella is famous in Egypt for its inconsistent taste.

Late last year, the state sold a majority stake in the firm to American-based Luxor Group and officials at Pyramids Breweries' former parent company said the group would overhaul the firm with the help of an international brewer.
Sawiris said Orascom's brewery would initially target customers in the tourist-rich areas of the Red Sea and southern Egypt before moving on to Cairo.

"Pyramids has about a 90 percent stake of the market while imported beers make up the remaining 10 percent. Our target is to take over most of the import market and then break into their (Pyramids) market. We have a head start because restructuring the firm will take time," he said.
